title: Do Llamas Work in English? On the Latent Language of Multilingual Transformers
why: Logit lens on Llama-2 shows a middle-layer detour through English; authors read it as an English-biased 'concept space'. Code: github.com/epfl-dlab/llm-latent-language.

title: Separating Tongue from Thought: Activation Patching Reveals Language-Agnostic Concept Representations in Transformers
why: Output language is fixed in the residual stream before the concept; averaging a concept's latent across languages improves translation. Only picturable nouns tested; culture-specific words explicitly left open.

title: The Semantic Hub Hypothesis: Language Models Share Semantic Representations Across Languages and Modalities
why: Shared representation space places equivalents near each other across languages/modalities; hub is anchored in the dominant language.

title: Do Multilingual LLMs Think In English?
why: Semantically loaded words (nouns/verbs) are routed through English latents; English steering vectors work better than target-language ones; Aya least English-routed. Reports tokens/word confound (EN ~1.4 vs FR/DE/NL ~2.0 for Llama-3.1-70B).

title: Beyond English-Centric LLMs: What Language Do Multilingual Language Models Think in?
why: Japanese-centric models (Swallow, LLM-jp) show dual Japanese+English latent languages, unlike Llama-2's English-only latent.

title: What Language(s) Does Aya-23 Think In? How Multilinguality Affects Internal Language Representations
why: Aya-23 activates typologically related languages during translation rather than a single English pivot: a candidate less English-centric comparison model.

title: How do Large Language Models Handle Multilingualism?
why: MWork hypothesis: understand -> think in English in middle layers -> generate in query language; language-specific neurons (PLND).

title: Language-Specific Neurons: The Key to Multilingual Capabilities in Large Language Models
why: LAPE identifies language-specific neurons; toggling them steers output language.

title: Language-Specific Latent Process Hinders Cross-Lingual Performance
why: Smaller models work mostly in an English-like shared space; larger ones drift to language-specific subspaces. Steering vector = mean(EN) - mean(non-EN) activations; pushing toward English helps small models.

title: Can you map it to English? The Role of Cross-Lingual Alignment in Multilingual Performance of LLMs
why: Instance-level alignment index (DALI); patching parallel English activations fixes some non-English errors; alignment necessary but not sufficient.

title: Language Defaults Before Content: A Causal Layer Map of Multilingual Generation
why: Donor-controlled patching across three LLMs: an English default signal appears in intermediate layers, content one layer later, target language last.

title: When Meanings Meet: Investigating the Emergence and Quality of Shared Concept Spaces during Multilingual Language Model Training
why: Shared concept space forms early in EuroLLM training, but rare concepts are weakly aligned (patching can hurt them) and averaging favours a dominant sense. Frequency is a real confound.

title: Large Language Models Share Representations of Latent Grammatical Concepts Across Typologically Diverse Languages
why: SAEs on Llama-3-8B/Aya-23-8B find grammatical features shared across languages; ablating them hurts all languages.

title: On the Language Neutrality of Pre-trained Multilingual Representations
why: Subtracting per-language centroids removes much language identity and improves cross-lingual retrieval. Justifies our language-mean removal.

title: It's not Greek to mBERT: Inducing Word-Level Translations from Multilingual BERT
why: Representations decompose into language-encoding and language-neutral components; method to extract both.

title: Universal Conceptual Structure in Neural Translation: Probing NLLB-200's Multilingual Geometry
why: Per-language centring removes language shifts; language identity sits in a compact subspace roughly orthogonal to concept structure.

title: Multilingual BERT has an accent: Evaluating English influences on fluency in multilingual models
why: Grammatical structures from English bleed into Spanish/Greek in mBERT ('grammatical structure bias'). Template for a controlled English-bias test.

title: Do Large Language Models Have an English 'Accent'? Evaluating and Improving the Naturalness of Multilingual LLMs
why: Corpus-level lexical/syntactic naturalness metrics show English-influenced patterns in French and Chinese LLM output.

authors: Havaldar, Rai, Singhal, Liu, Guntuku, Ungar
title: Multilingual Language Models are not Multicultural: A Case Study in Emotion
why: Emotion words embedded via 'I feel X'/'I am X'; in multilingual models non-English emotion embeddings drift toward English ones, and explicit alignment pulls them further.

title: Emotions Where Art Thou: Understanding and Characterizing the Emotional Latent Space of Large Language Models
why: Low-dimensional emotional subspace in Llama-3.1 that generalises across five languages; valence/arousal-like axes.

title: Discovering Lexical Gaps Using Embeddings from Multilingual LLMs
why: Korean-English emotion adjectives in 'I am X' frames; gap words have lower nearest-neighbour (CSLS) similarity; classifiers reach AUC ~0.81 (KO->EN) / 0.76 (EN->KO); unaligned spaces beat Procrustes-aligned. Frequency and tokenisation not controlled.

title: Language Unalignability: Why Some Concepts Resist Cross-Cultural Benchmark Evaluation
why: Position paper: concepts as 'usage clouds' of contextual embeddings; alpha-unalignability; proposed metrics (cycle consistency, curvature mismatch, representation-intervention gap). Mostly untested; useful vocabulary.

title: Crowdsourcing Lexical Diversity
why: LingoGap crowdsourcing for lexical gaps in domains like kinship and food; documents LLM errors on gap words.

title: Using Linguistic Typology to Enrich Multilingual Lexicons: the Case of Lexical Gaps in Kinship
why: Kinship gap data for many languages: a source of ground-truth gaps beyond 'famous untranslatables'.

title: Language Diversity: Visible to Humans, Exploitable by Machines
why: Universal Knowledge Core represents lexical gaps explicitly across 1000+ languages.

title: Locally Measuring Cross-lingual Lexical Alignment: A Domain and Word Level Perspective
why: Word/domain-level alignment metrics validated with kinship lexical gaps.

title: Linear Algebraic Structure of Word Senses, with Applications to Polysemy
why: Word vectors are linear superpositions of senses recoverable by sparse coding: theoretical precedent for 'recipe' decomposition.

title: The Geometry of Categorical and Hierarchical Concepts in Large Language Models
why: Extends the linear representation hypothesis to categorical/hierarchical concepts as vectors and polytopes.

title: LEACE: Perfect linear concept erasure in closed form
why: Closed-form least-squares concept erasure (used to remove stance/language identity).

title: Eliciting Latent Predictions from Transformers with the Tuned Lens
why: Tuned lens: learned affine read-out per layer; more reliable than the logit lens, especially in early layers.

title: On the Limitations of Unsupervised Bilingual Dictionary Induction
why: Embedding spaces of different languages are not isomorphic, even for close pairs: a caution for any 'geometry is universal' claim.

title: Benchmarking Concept-Spilling Across Languages in LLMs
why: When asked for five meanings of polysemous words in nine languages, models fall back on dominant-language meanings ('language spilling'). Close to our distinction-collapse test.

title: Towards Effective Disambiguation for Machine Translation with Large Language Models
why: LLMs vs NMT on ambiguous words (DiBiMT); NMT systems biased toward frequent senses.

title: Benchmarking LLM-based Machine Translation on Cultural Awareness
why: CAMT dataset of culture-specific items; prompting the model to explain items improves understandability.

title: Cross-linguistic disagreement as a conflict of semantic alignment norms in multilingual AI
why: Names the tension between cross-lingual consistency and language-specific 'folk' semantics. Useful framing for the bid.

title: Crosslingual Transfer Learning for Low-Resource Languages Based on Multilingual Colexification Graphs
why: Colexification patterns for 2,000+ concepts across 1,335 languages mined from parallel text.

title: The Platonic Representation Hypothesis
why: Argues representations converge toward a shared model of reality. The 'universal representation' claim our experiments test against.

title: Revisiting the Platonic Representation Hypothesis: An Aristotelian View
why: Similarity metrics are inflated by scale; proposes permutation-based null calibration. Use for chance baselines.

title: A theory of platonic representations in language models
why: Synthetic-grammar account of why cross-lingual similarity peaks in middle layers and grows with language proximity.

title: Lost in Translation: Large Language Models in Non-English Content Analysis
why: Policy report: English-dominant training transfers English assumptions to other languages (e.g. connotations of 'dove').

title: Testing the Deliteralization Hypothesis in Human and Machine Translation
why: Human translations remain less literal than all tested MT/LLM systems across 54 language pairs.

title: Do GPTs Produce Less Literal Translations?
why: GPT translations out of English are less literal than NMT at similar quality.

title: Analyzing Uncertainty in Neural Machine Translation
why: Separates intrinsic uncertainty (many valid translations) from extrinsic (noisy data); models over-spread probability mass; releases multi-reference data.

title: Uncertainty Determines the Adequacy of the Mode and the Tractability of Decoding in Sequence-to-Sequence Models
why: Measures intrinsic uncertainty as agreement among multiple references; ambiguous inputs give flatter distributions and more search errors.

title: Semantic Uncertainty: Linguistic Invariances for Uncertainty Estimation in Natural Language Generation
why: Entropy over meaning clusters (bidirectional entailment) rather than strings.

title: Kernel Language Entropy: Fine-grained Uncertainty Quantification for LLMs from Semantic Similarities
why: Von Neumann entropy of a unit-trace semantic kernel; generalises semantic entropy without hard clusters.

title: Fine-Grained Uncertainty Decomposition in Large Language Models: A Spectral Approach
why: Kernel/von Neumann decomposition into aleatoric and epistemic parts.

title: Distinguishing the Knowable from the Unknowable with Language Models
why: A larger model stands in for ground truth; linear probes on the small model's activations predict epistemic tokens (AUC ~0.94 in-distribution).

title: To Believe or Not to Believe Your LLM
why: Information-theoretic test for when only epistemic uncertainty is large, via iterative prompting with the model's own previous answers.

authors: Hou, Liu, Qian, Andreas, Chang, Zhang
title: Decomposing Uncertainty for Large Language Models through Input Clarification Ensembling
why: Ensemble over clarifications of the input: MI between output and clarification = ambiguity (aleatoric); expected entropy after clarification = remainder. Template for our gloss test.

title: The Anatomy of Uncertainty in LLMs
why: Three components (input ambiguity, knowledge gaps, decoding randomness), each estimated by varying one factor; explicitly non-additive diagnostics.

title: Complementing Self-Consistency with Cross-Model Disagreement for Uncertainty Quantification
why: Cross-model disagreement as an epistemic term; flags confident failures; caveats about uneven competence and stylistic divergence across model families.

title: Quantifying Aleatoric and Epistemic Uncertainty in Machine Learning: Are Conditional Entropy and Mutual Information Appropriate Measures?
why: Argues the entropy/MI additive decomposition has incoherencies; MI is closer to divergence than ignorance.

title: Aleatoric and Epistemic Uncertainty in Machine Learning: An Introduction to Concepts and Methods
why: Standard reference for the two notions.

title: Why machine learning models fail to fully capture epistemic uncertainty
why: Aleatoric estimates are only trustworthy when epistemic uncertainty is low; common methods confuse the two. Directly relevant to dialect texts.

title: (title: see arXiv 2606.12646) non-partition theorem for aleatoric/epistemic uncertainty
why: Argues 'reducible' depends on the acquisition class; splits epistemic into sample-reducible and mechanism-reducible. Maps onto 'more data' vs 'a gloss'.

title: Rethinking Aleatoric and Epistemic Uncertainty
why: Argues the aleatoric/epistemic dichotomy is too simple for ML; proposes a finer vocabulary.

title: Uncertainty in Natural Language Generation: From Theory to Applications
why: Principled treatment of uncertainty in NLG, including support for multiple valid outputs and perspectives.

title: What Comes Next? Evaluating Uncertainty in Neural Text Generators Against Human Production Variability
why: Uses variability across human productions as the reference for aleatoric uncertainty: model for using multiple human translations.

title: Trick or Neat: Adversarial Ambiguity and Language Model Evaluation
why: Prompting fails to detect ambiguity robustly, but linear probes on hidden states decode it with high accuracy (sometimes >90%).

title: Beyond the Final Layer: Intermediate Representations for Better Multilingual Calibration in Large Language Models
why: Non-English calibration is systematically worse, especially low-resource; intermediate layers help.

title: Investigating the Multilingual Calibration Effects of Language Model Instruction-Tuning
why: Instruction tuning makes models overconfident on low-resource languages.

title: On the Calibration of Massively Multilingual Language Models
why: mBERT/XLM-R are miscalibrated zero-shot on low-resource and typologically distant languages.

title: Quantifying the Dialect Gap and its Correlates Across Languages
why: Dialect performance gaps in MT/ASR; proximity to a well-resourced dialect is the strongest predictor.

title: DialectBench: A NLP Benchmark for Dialects, Varieties, and Closely-Related Languages
why: Benchmark and a relative dialect-gap metric.

title: Dictionary-based Phrase-level Prompting of Large Language Models for Machine Translation
why: Putting dictionary candidates in the prompt helps rare words in low-resource MT: evidence that glosses reduce epistemic uncertainty.

title: Teaching Large Language Models an Unseen Language on the Fly
why: DiPMT++: dictionary plus 5K parallel sentences takes GPT-4 from 0 to 16 BLEU on Chinese->Zhuang.

title: A Benchmark for Learning to Translate a New Language from One Grammar Book
why: MTOB: English-Kalamang from a grammar book in context.

title: Can LLMs Really Learn to Translate a Low-Resource Language from One Grammar Book?
why: Finds most MTOB gains come from parallel examples rather than grammatical explanation.

title: Translationese as a Rational Response to Translation Task Difficulty
why: Uses translation-solution entropy H(T|S) as a difficulty measure: a bridge to translation-process research (word translation entropy).

title: Large language models effectively leverage document-level context for literary translation, but critical errors persist
why: Paragraph-level LLM literary translation beats sentence-level, but critical errors and voice loss persist.
